transcript:
This message is from Synchrony Bank, who wants to remind you to stay flexible.
Not the 10,000 steps before breakfast, yoga bending, circus performing, wish I hadn't done that kind of flexible.
It's about staying financially flexible, like with their high-yield savings account.
You'll earn a great rate without monthly fees or minimums that can slow your progress.
Go to Synchrony.com/NPR. Member FDIC.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. A federal judge ordered President Trump to immediately restore access for three news outlets banned from the White House.
It appears David Falkenflick reports it's in the temporary ruling.
The judge found the administration revoked access without due process and likely violated CNN, MS Now, and Politico's constitutional rights.
U.S. District Court Judge Timothy Kelly ruled that the administration had violated the journalists' rights to due process.
No warning, no ability to appeal.
He swatted aside the Justice Department's claims involving national security, so shortly after midnight he issued a temporary restraining order.
But journalists for all three outlets said they arrived in the morning only to be kept out again.
So Judge Kelly demanded answers, and suddenly access was restored.
CNN's status in the TV pool remains unclear.
Five networks share the burden and cost of presenting all the president's public remarks.
An official with one of those networks said none of the networks would present video until the White House offered written assurances for CNN.
The official spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorized to comment publicly.
David Falkenflick, NPR News.
The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate rose this week above 7 percent for the first time since January 2025,
the latest affordability setback for prospective homebuyers.
NPR's Stephen Besaha has more on why it's happening now.
OK, stop me if you've heard this one before. It goes back to the U.S. war against Iran.
The war has played a big part in driving up mortgage rates by driving up the cost of oil and with it inflation.
Inflation concerns go up, bond yields go up, and mortgage rates tend to follow.
And remember, the bond market influences borrowing costs all across the economy, including for homes.
There's also a bunch of other factors hitting the bond market like all at once right now.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reporting President Trump's nominee to lead the FDA is voicing support for the safety of vaccines during a Senate hearing.
That puts Dr. Heidi Overton out of step with her potential new boss, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
Currently serving as White House adviser, Overton has worked on Trump administration health efforts.
A new analysis of census data finds the poverty rate for seniors has risen for the fifth year in a row.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports older, lower income adults are struggling to save for retirement.
The AARP Foundation analysis found women are far more likely than men to age into poverty.
And its own survey found just under a third of those 50 to 64 reported a significant drop in household income in the past three months.
Foundation President Claire Casey says even a small disruption like a car breaking down can be devastating for low income workers.
You're much more likely to end up in the long term unemployed and you're much more likely to end up in a job that makes less than the one you were in.
A third of older low income adults also said they did not have enough savings to cover an emergency expense of $100.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
U.S. stocks have slowed their rallies since the S&P 500 climbed to the brink of its all time high earlier this week. This is NPR.
The Energy Department says it will spend almost $2 billion to try to squeeze more electricity out of the nation's aging power grid.
It comes amid skyrocketing energy demand spurred by AI.
The money will go toward 31 projects across 26 states that are expected to produce more than 23 gigawatts of additional electricity capacity, enough to power 16 million homes.
California's highest court has ruled that a Republican sheriff illegally seized hundreds of thousands of ballots earlier this year and must return them.
The ballots were from a vote on whether to redraw California's congressional map to favor Democrats.
From Member Station KVCR, Madison Ahmet reports.
Sheriff Chad Bianco of Riverside County, about 60 miles east of Los Angeles, said he took the ballots from the county registrar to investigate alleged voter fraud.
State and county elections officials said there was no evidence of fraud.
California's Attorney General Rob Bonta told Bianco to pause the investigation.
In its rulings, the court says Bianco bypassed election law by taking the ballots and defied Bonta's authority.
Bonta says the rulings help protect election integrity.
The Riverside County Sheriff is not above the law, and state law must be enforced.
Bianco says he's disappointed by the rulings, but will comply with them.
For NPR News, I'm Madison Ahmet in San Bernardino.
Chinese President Xi Jinping says two giant pandas from China will arrive at a zoo at Zoo Atlanta in the coming days.
Their arrival will bolster a loan program that at one time lapsed as part of tensions between Beijing and Washington.
The pandas are Ping Ping, a male, and Fu Shuang, a female.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Charles Schwab with their original podcast, Choiceology.
Choiceology is a show about the psychology and economics behind people's decisions.
Download the latest episode and subscribe at Schwab.com/podcast.
